claims.about: PHP / Laravel (php-laravel) compared with other stacks
claims.measured: Single DB query: php-laravel 149 req/s on 1 CPU; go-gin 22,138; node-express 9,034; bun-elysia 31,596
claims.why: Laravel measured about 60–200 times slower than the other stacks on the same 1-CPU endpoint, so on 2 vCPUs the framework alone caps throughput near 300 req/s, well short of the 3,000 needed.

claims.claim: A typical uncached Laravel endpoint with a database query costs roughly 10–30 ms of CPU.
claims.measured: 149 req/s at 94% of 1 CPU on the single-query test, about 6.3 ms of CPU per request; p50 latency 410 ms under 64 connections
claims.why: The 10 ms lower bound is within 2x of the measured ~6.3 ms, though the range as a whole is pessimistic.

claims.claim: Two vCPUs therefore give you about 100–300 requests per second at best.
claims.measured: 149 req/s on 1 CPU (single DB query), so about 300 req/s on 2 vCPU
claims.why: Scaling the 1-CPU figure by two gives about 300 req/s, which matches the top of the claimed range.

claims.claim: A Go or Node rewrite might be several times faster.
claims.about: go-gin / go-nethttp / node-express / node-fastify vs php-laravel
claims.measured: Single DB query: go-gin 22,138, go-nethttp 19,543, node-fastify 9,423, node-express 9,034 vs php-laravel 149 req/s (about 60–150x); plaintext: go-gin 53,941 vs 681 (about 79x)
claims.why: The direction is right, but the measured gap is roughly 60–150 times, far more than 'several times'.

claims.claim: Just a bigger server alone only buys a small multiple, not the 30x or more you need.
claims.about: php-laravel capacity on the current 2 vCPU server
claims.measured: About 300 req/s on 2 vCPU for a DB-backed endpoint (149 per CPU), so 3,000 req/s needs about 10x
claims.why: Measured Laravel throughput means about a 10x increase is needed, not 30x; the 30x figure comes from the low 100 req/s estimate.

claims.claim: Laravel Octane (Swoole or RoadRunner) is faster and still PHP.
claims.measured: Plaintext 1,172 vs 681; JSON 1,224 vs 705; single DB query 732 vs 149; 20 queries 123 vs 93; but 10 ms I/O wait 86 vs 591
claims.why: Octane measured faster on every test except the I/O-wait one, where it was much slower.

claims.measured: Peak memory 100–116 MB vs 58–75 MB for php-laravel within 15 s runs
claims.why: Short runs show higher memory use but nothing about growth over time or leaks.

claims.claim: Password hashing is deliberately CPU-heavy; a few hundred logins per second will overwhelm 2 vCPUs.
claims.why: No password-hashing or login workload was measured.

claims.claim: With about 4 GB, pm.max_children is probably 30–40 depending on memory per worker.
claims.measured: php-laravel container peak 58–75 MB, worker count not stated
claims.why: The measurements give whole-container memory with an unknown number of workers, so memory per worker can't be worked out.
